 1   Resolution Number 6165, by Senator Peralta, 

 2   commemorating the 206th anniversary of Colombia's 

 3   Declaration of Independence on July 20, 2016.

 4                ACTING PRESIDENT AKSHAR:   Senator 

 5   Peralta.

 6                SENATOR PERALTA:   Thank you, 

 7   Mr. President.

 8                This year marks the 206th year of 

 9   Colombian independence.  Colombia celebrates 

10   Independence Day each year on July 20th.  The day 

11   commemorates the Declaration of Independence made 

12   on the date in 1810.  That day, almost 206 years 

13   ago, the citizens of Bogota, Colombia, Colombia's 

14   capital, created their first representative 

15   council, an action that led to Colombia's first 

16   national government.  

17                Even though it took another nine 

18   years to achieve full independence from Spain, 

19   Colombians annually celebrate the first "El Grito 

20   de Independencia," or "Cry for Independence," led 

21   by Simón Bolívar.  Complete victory over Spain 

22   was declared in August of 1819.  

23                Colombian independence is an 

24   occasion of great celebration in my district, 

25   which is home to La Pequeña Colombia, or "Little 


                                                                3536

 1   Colombia," and generations of Colombians and 

 2   Colombian families, including the actor and 

 3   comedian John Leguizamo, who grew up in 

 4   Jackson Heights.  La Pequeña Colombia is right at 

 5   the heart of my district -- which, as you know, 

 6   is the United Nations of all Senate districts.  

 7                Like the United States, Colombia has 

 8   also a long tradition of constitutional 

 9   government.  The United States and Colombia are 

10   good friends, they are allies, a relationship 

11   forged by a love of democracy, the rule of law, 

12   and of course liberty.  

13                By way of this resolution, we extend 

14   our best wishes to our Colombian-American friends 

15   across the state in advance of this important and 

16   joyful day.

17                Thank you, Mr. President.

11                SENATOR SQUADRON:   To explain my 

12   vote, Mr. President.

13                Certainly inciting violence against 

14   an active member of the military is an absolutely 

15   unacceptable act and one that we should 

16   universally condemn.  

17                Like a nearly identical bill 

18   pertaining to police officers earlier in the 

19   session, this bill has a standard just pulled 

20   verbatim from a Supreme Court decision:  "Such 

21   advocacy is directed to inciting or producing 

22   imminent lawless action and is likely to incite 

23   or produce such action."  That's the definition.  

24   That is not a definition that law enforcement, 

25   prosecutors, courts are going to be able to use 


                                                                3540

 1   effectively.

 2                Passing a law with a very important 

 3   positive headline that's going to take years and 

 4   millions of dollars in litigation to actually 

 5   understand and enforce doesn't do anyone any 

 6   favors.  We should make a clear statement against 

 7   inciting violence against active-duty military, 

 8   absolutely, but we should do it in a way that has 

 9   meaning, not in a way that's going to create 

10   endless litigation based on the copying verbatim 

11   of a Supreme Court decision without putting any 

12   flesh on those bones.  

13                I unfortunately have to vote no, 

14   Mr. President.
